transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
Five men have been arrested near a British Air Force base after reports of three suspicious
vehicles in the area.
The base has been used in limited capacity by U.S. bombers staged for the war with Iran.
The five are being held under the country's explosive act, but police have not said publicly
whether the arrests are connected to the base.
Iran says only diplomacy can end the U.S. war with Iran.
This comes after President Trump Friday rejected an Iranian proposal to re-open the Strait
of Hormuz and stop the fighting.
Trump says Tehran's offer isn't acceptable, and he made that decision as midterm elections
approach.
NPR's Mara Lison has more.
The war is very unpopular, even with Republican voters.
There is now a small but growing number of Republicans in Congress coming out against
the war.
And the war isn't just unpopular with voters because they believe Trump when he said he
wouldn't get into any foreign wars.
Some of them voted for him because of that promise.
It's also unpopular because voters see a direct connection between the war and higher
gas prices, higher diesel prices, and we know that the cost of living is the number one
issue in this election over and beyond anything else.
That's NPR's Mara Lison with our story.
Fuel prices, meanwhile, remain high.
With the average cost for gasoline right now at $4.48 a gallon, diesel sits at $6.47 a
gallon.
In Hawaii, Hurricane Nolo continues to move away from the island chain.
The storm has now become a major hurricane with wind speeds topping 111 miles an hour.
But as Hawaii Public Radio's Bill Dorman reports, the increasing wind speeds are not causing
major damage.
The storm's impacts are lingering.
Strong and gusty winds are whipping across several islands, especially Maui and Hawaii
Island.
That's knocked out power to several thousand people, and floodwaters have swept through
some areas.
Even so, the storm did not cause as much damage as feared.
Hurricane Nolo is expected to reach its peak intensity Monday, even further from Hawaii's
shores.
For NPR News, I'm Bill Dorman in Honolulu.
Pope Leo told a massive crowd gathered at the Shrine of Lourdes Sunday that the Catholic
Church must confront deep wounds caused by a clergy abuse.
As NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports, Leo is on a four-day visit to France.
Lourdes is a town in the foothills of the Pyrenees Mountains that attracts some three
million pilgrims a year for its purported healing springwaters on the spot where a 19th-century
shepherd girl had apparitions of Virgin Mary.
The site is also connected to a recent scandal.
The shrine's facade has a series of mosaics by a prominent religious artist accused of
abusing 20 women.
The story's tall mosaics have been covered for the pope's visit.
Leo has previously apologized for abuse scandals that have damaged the church's credibility.
On a trip to Spain in June, he told bishops they must listen to survivors and offer reparations.
Eleanor Beardsley in Pierre News, Paris.
And you're listening to NPR News.
Russian and Ukrainian forces traded more attacks this weekend.
At least eight people were killed in Ukraine, and one died in Russia.
Moscow is continuing to attack Ukraine's cities, often hitting apartment buildings and killing
civilians.
Ukraine strikes primarily target Russia's oil refineries.
News in Switzerland have resoundingly defeated a proposal to make their traditional neutrality
more strict.
Imogene Folks reports from Bern.
The result?
70% of those voting rejected the proposals suggest most Swiss believe neutrality cannot
ignore international law or reward aggression.
And that to protect their own country, new alliances with European neighbors may be necessary.
They also doubted the motivations of a key supporter of strict neutrality, right-wing
political and business leader Christoph Blocher.
His companies traded with Apartheid South Africa and were trading with Russia until sanctions
were imposed.
For NPR News, I'm Imogene Folks in Bern.
Florida made a big jump in this week's college football rankings.
After handily beating Ole Miss on Saturday, the Gators climbed 13 places to land in number
eight.
Texas, Georgia, and Notre Dame continued their hold on the top three spots, while Miami made
it to number four.
Ohio State moved up two spots to number five, while Indiana dropped one place despite a
win on Saturday, landing in the number six slot.
Alabama is in seventh, while after a major loss, Ole Miss just dropped slightly to number
nine with BYU in tenth.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Five men arrested near British Air Force base after reports of suspicious vehicles in area
President Trump rejects Iranian proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz and stop fighting
War with Iran remains unpopular with voters and growing number of Republican Congress members
Average gasoline price reaches $4.48 per gallon, diesel at $6.47 per gallon
Hurricane Nolo becomes major hurricane with 111 mph winds, moving away from Hawaiian islands
Pope Leo tells crowd at Shrine of Lourdes that Catholic Church must confront clergy abuse
Russian and Ukrainian forces trade attacks; at least eight killed in Ukraine, one in Russia
Swiss voters reject proposal to make traditional neutrality more strict with 70 percent voting no
Florida Gators climb 13 places to number eight in college football rankings after beating Ole Miss
